newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds Chemist Q2 sales up 8.9 percent.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds Chemist Q2 sales up 8.9 percent.

text.p: British high street retail chain Lloyds Chemist Plc said on Tuesday that overall sales in the second quarter were 8.9 percent up on the same period a year ago and rose 8.5 percent in the second half from the previous level.

In a statement, Lloyds said pressures from a bid process as British drugs wholesaler and retailer UniChem and German pharmaceutical group Gehe vie for control of the company, continued to affect group profits adversely.
Lloyds said chemist sales in the half year were up 3.5 percent on a year ago while those at its Holland & Barrett health food chain rose 16.8 percent.
It said that pharmaceutical sales gained 11.7 percent in the half year from a year ago and veterinary sales shot up 21.4 percent, but health and beauty sales slipped 2.6 percent.

Lloyds said in its chemist business, sales of colds and flu remedies increased in the final two weeks of the second quarter but there was no repeat of 1995's flu epidemic which boosted both prescriptions and cash sales.
The company said that costs had been incurred across the group in order to ensure the retention of key staff at all levels pending conclusion of the bid process.
Lloyds shares were unchanged at 514 pence by 1624 GMT.
Property disposal costs are expected to be broadly in line with the previous year, Lloyds said.
Lloyds chairman Allen Lloyd said the disruptive effects of the bid process, which has lasted for almost a year, "have continued to have a negative impact upon the first half of the current year."
Lloyd said in October 1996 that uncertainty and costs associated with the bids had adversely affected second half financial results.
Gehe and UniChem both launched bids early in 1995 but these lapsed after being referred to Britain's competition authority, the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC).
The MMC called for disposals of certain parts of Lloyds business if either Gehe or UniChem gained control.
Both predators then relaunched bids and cannot increase these until after January 17.
Lloyds said it would advise shareholders which offer to accept "shortly after that date."
UniChem's cash and shares offer values Lloyds at 657.6 million stg, while Gehe is offering 500 pence per share in cash.
